rulings.model: The IRS makes the election optional ('You may be able to claim ... By making this election') and says that if made, 'You can't carry over to or from any other year any foreign taxes paid or accrued in a tax year to which the election applies'. The program elects automatically whenever the conditions are met. This forfeits any 2025 excess that Form 1116 would carry back or forward. The restatement's 'never less' reasoning covers only the current-year credit.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.f1116_carryover_election and coordinator decision D3 (docs/provisional/DECISIONS.md, X1-F1116: the election made whenever its conditions are met). i1116 pp. 1-2: with the election "You can't carry over to or from any other year any foreign taxes". The model reads the election as the filer's choice and notes that electing forfeits any excess of foreign tax over the regular tax that Form 1116 would carry forward. The recorded reading and D3 make the election whenever available; on this tool's Form 1116 path any such excess refuses (f1116.carryover_out, coordinator decision D1), so a No could only refuse the return. The English states what the project does. Raised for the owner in the report: whether to refuse instead of electing when ftc.taxes exceeds ftc.regular_tax, which keeps the carryforward the election forfeits.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; medium; i1040gi (2025), Schedule 3, line 1, condition 4 for the credit without Form 1116: "You aren't filing Form 4563 or excluding income from sources within Puerto Rico." The rendered conditions match i1116's three, which do not repeat it, and ftc.needs1116 does not test it; sa.excluded_income (asked of every filer) refuses only on Schedule A, Schedule 1-A, sli and other credits, not on ftc, so a Form 4563 filer or Puerto Rico excluder with foreign tax of $300 or less ($600 joint) gets the election credit (BUG-0769). Fix: add sa.excluded_income = true to ftc.needs1116's failed conditions, sending the return to Form 1116, where f1116.reduction refuses.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; screens scope.other_line16 and scope.credits. i1116 p. 25, Line 20, "Individuals. Enter the total of Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR, line 16, and Schedule 2 (Form 1040), Part I, line 1z, less any tax included on line 16 from Form 4972." and "If you file Form 8978, Partner’s Additional Reporting Year Tax, you will need to increase or decrease the amount you report on Form 1116, line 20 ... If, after your adjustment, the amount of your tax is zero or less, enter -0- on Form 1116, line 20." The restatement is the BUG-0190 fix (round-1 F1): ftc.regular_tax = f1040.line16 + s2.line1z. The three omitted terms are refused. Form 4972: scope.other_line16 ("... including filing Form 8814 (even with no tax), Form 4972, Form 8615, a section 962 election, Form 8621, a Form 8978 amount ...") refuses f1040.line16 and scope.ready, so no Form 4972 tax is in line 16 and nothing is subtracted. Form 8978: a positive amount is in line 16 and refused by the same screen; a negative one goes to Schedule 3 Part I and is refused by scope.credits ("... any other amount for Schedule 3 Part I (for example a Form 8978 adjustment)", at f1040 lines 29 and 30). The zero floor applies only "after your adjustment"; without one, line 16 and line 1z are both NonNegDollars, so their sum is never below zero. The fix uses line 1z, not line 3, which agrees with the page (line 3 adds the alternative minimum tax, section 26(b)(2)). Regression stage18.ftc_limit_with_repayment evaluates to ftc.regular_tax $375.00, ftc.credit $200.00 and Form 1040 line 22 $175.00, the round-1 source values. No new error found.
